visual_action: A montage shows a large crowd of people participating in a street protest in an urban setting, identified by on-screen text as Washington, D.C. The protesters, who are diverse in age and race, are marching, holding many large banners and handmade signs, and some appear to be chanting. The weather appears overcast and cool, with participants wearing winter clothing.

cast.name: Unnamed protesters
cast.evidence: The entire video consists of footage of a large group of unidentified people marching in a protest.

cast.name: Democratic Party
cast.evidence: The video was posted by the official @democrats account, which frames the event and presents it to the audience.

on_screen_text.text: The People's March in Washington, D.C.
TOGETHER WE CAN TOGETHER WE WILL
The Power of the People Is Stronger than The People in Power - Resist !
KEEP YOUR POLITICS OFF MY BODY
WE ONLY LOSE IF WE STOP FIGHTING

spoken_summary: The audio consists of the lyrics from the song "labour" by Paris Paloma. A female vocalist sings, "It's not an act of love, if you make her, you make me do too much labor. All day, every day, therapist, mother, maintenance, then a virgin, nurse, then a servant," describing the exhaustive and contradictory roles expected of women.
audio_music: The video is set to the song 'labour' by Paris Paloma, which plays throughout. The track has an anthemic and powerful feel, with strong female vocals that build in intensity, creating an effect of empowerment and solidarity that matches the protest visuals.
editing_pacing: The video is a montage with quick cuts between various scenes from the protest march, showing different groups of people, signs, and angles. The pacing is dynamic and energetic.
cultural_references: The song 'labour' by Paris Paloma, which went viral on TikTok as an anthem expressing female exhaustion and rage.
central_claim: A large and powerful movement of people gathered in Washington D.C. for 'The People's March' to demand women's rights, including reproductive freedom and equal rights.
intended_effect: To inspire viewers with the scale and energy of the women's rights movement and to signal solidarity with the cause.
